summary.text: A volcanic island is an island of volcanic origin, sometimes called a high island to set it apart from low islands made of sediment or uplifted coral reef.
Volcanic islands normally rise above a hotspot or a subduction zone, and many climb from the deep ocean floor to rough, mountainous interiors.
They are more likely to be habitable than low islands, since larger islands usually hold fresh groundwater, but they face hazards from eruptions to tsunamis and typhoons.

facts.label: Where they form
facts.value: Above a hotspot or subduction zone

facts.label: Surrounding reefs
facts.value: Fringing or barrier reefs that create lagoons

items.prompt: Settlers must pick between a low island of sand and coral and a sizeable volcanic island nearby. Which is more likely to give them fresh groundwater?

options.label: The low sand and coral island
The sizeable volcanic island
Both are equally likely
Neither ever has groundwater

items.explain: Islands above a certain size usually have fresh groundwater while low islands often do not, so volcanic islands are more likely to be habitable.

items.prompt: Volcanic islands are called 'high islands'. Does that mean every one stands taller than every 'low island'?

options.label: Yes, with no exceptions
Yes, low ones stay under 10 m
No, some are under 1 m tall
No, low ones are always taller

items.explain: The names describe how the islands formed: some volcanic islets rise no more than 1 m, while low islands such as Nauru and Niue rise over 50 m.

items.prompt: On many volcanic islands, villages crowd along the shore and the middle stays nearly empty. What helps explain this?

options.label: The interior is always an active crater
Laws ban building away from the sea
The interior has no rain at all
Dense forest and rugged interiors limit settlement

items.explain: Rough, mountainous interiors often covered by dense tropical forest limit inland settlement, pushing communities to the coast.

items.prompt: A volcanic island wants to protect its coast from storm surges using a nature-based approach. What would that involve?

options.label: Restoring mangroves or coral reefs offshore
Building a tall concrete sea wall
Moving every town to the summit
Dredging deeper channels near shore

items.explain: Nature-based solutions use natural systems, such as restored mangroves or coral reefs, to shield against tsunamis and storm surges.

items.prompt: Geologists want to guess where a brand-new volcanic island might someday appear. Which setting is the best bet?

options.label: The middle of a stable continent
A sandbar at a river mouth
Over a hotspot in the ocean
The calm lagoon inside an atoll

items.explain: Volcanic islands normally rise above a hotspot or a subduction zone.

items.prompt: Larger volcanic islands often have rivers. What problem can those rivers bring?

options.label: They dry out the island's groundwater
They cause flooding and coastal erosion
They set off volcanic eruptions
They make the island sink faster

items.explain: Rivers on larger islands bring flood hazards and carry sediment that shapes the coast and contributes to erosion.
